wiki-iran.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Iran — a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking the country up, and one that rises when a decision made in Tehran or about Tehran reaches an audience far beyond it.
wiki-iran.recent: Attention has drifted down through August even as the pressure rose: Treasury Secretary Bessent named the sanctions campaign "Economic Outcast" and Treasury listed nearly 60 entities on Monday, binding third countries, and the rial opened at 2.02 million per dollar. Rezaei then warned that "not even one drop" would leave Hormuz, before opening a temporary corridor.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the benchmark most of the world's oil is priced against. It moves on supply — a strike, a sanction, a strait — and fuel, freight and fertiliser move after it.
brent.recent: Brent sits near $88 after peaking at $105.30 on Jul 23, with Iran's threat to shut the Strait of Hormuz — one gas carrier transited on Monday — failing to push prices higher. China cut oil imports 45%, and inventories absorbed the chokepoint before price did. Washington's widened sanctions campaign has not yet bitten.

wti.standing: The price of a barrel of West Texas Intermediate, the light, low-sulphur crude that sets the American benchmark. It is priced inland at Cushing, Oklahoma, and it feeds through to US pump prices, refining margins and freight costs.
wti.recent: The war-risk premium built in August has drained away. Prices ran above $91 in mid-August after Trump signalled he would not renew the Iran deal and the US threatened an indefinite blockade, with Hormuz traffic falling to single digits as the 60-day MoU deadline expired. They have since retreated: China cut oil imports 45%, absorbing the chokepoint through inventory rather than price.

natgas-hh.standing: The U.S. benchmark price for natural gas, set at a Louisiana pipeline hub and used to price most American gas contracts. It sets what households pay to heat and cook, what power plants pay to run, and what fertiliser and chemical makers pay for feedstock.
natgas-hh.recent: Gas has drifted down about 12% over two months, from $3.34 on Jun 30 to $2.70, with the floor at $2.56 on Aug 7. Supply news has run the same direction: Pakistan Petroleum struck gas in Chiltan rock at Sujawal, and Iran reported 161 billion cubic meters recoverable in Fars province.

wheat.standing: The world reference price for a tonne of milling wheat, the grain behind bread and flour across most of the world. It moves on harvests, war and export policy, and food bills in importing countries move after it.
wheat.recent: Wheat has climbed roughly a third since September 2025, peaking in July 2026. Drought across Europe has run the Rhine low enough to expose beaches at Nijmegen and burn British fields brown, while Russia and Ukraine have struck each other's export infrastructure — the rail station at the Danube grain port of Izmail among them. Sindh will import 5 million tons.

rice.standing: The world price of milled rice, the staple grain for more than half the planet. It is set by a thin export market — a handful of Asian shippers — so a single country's export ban or a good monsoon moves what billions pay to eat.
rice.recent: Rice has fallen 17.7% over the series, from a high of $563.8 in Aug 2024 to $330.6 in Oct 2025 before recovering to $464. The move is a supply story the coverage does not directly explain, though it sits alongside yield work in Bangkok, where two purple non-sulfur bacteria strains raised Jasmine rice yields.

copper.standing: The world price of refined copper, the metal that carries electricity in almost everything that uses it. Grids, motors, buildings and cables all bid for the same supply, so its price tracks how fast the world is wiring itself.
copper.recent: Copper sits near the top of its range, up about half over the series and just under the June 2026 high of $13,550 a tonne. The demand story is electrical: AI data centres are straining transformer design, electric vehicles are pushing grid voltage limits, and Washington has now banned foreign-made grid parts, tightening a supply chain already short of copper. In Zambia, a top producer, Hichilema won a second term with 60% of the vote.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, and the benchmark that sits under mortgages, corporate loans and the pricing of nearly every other asset. It rises when investors demand more compensation for inflation or risk.
us-10y.recent: The long end of the curve has repriced: thirty-year yields reached 5.3%, a level last seen in 2007, and the Treasury doubled its long-bond buyback in response. Tariffs and war are the inputs — the Yale Budget Lab puts the tariff effect on consumer prices at roughly 0.7% — and on $40 trillion of debt, each tenth of a point costs about $40 billion a year.

sp500.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of 500 large US-listed companies, and the benchmark most equity money in the world is measured against. Trillions in pension and index funds track it, so its level sets what ordinary retirement savings are worth.
sp500.recent: The index sits near its 62-day high after a run driven by AI capital spending and the vendor financing behind it: Nvidia pledged $500 billion to its own buyers, a commitment BofA reiterated its rating on. The counterweight came from rates and retail — Fed minutes showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, and Walmart's results hit retail stocks on 20 August.

nasdaq100.standing: A stock index tracking the 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange, weighted by market value. It is dominated by a handful of technology firms, so it moves less on the broad economy than on what a few chipmakers and platforms report.
nasdaq100.recent: The index sits below its early-June high after a July trough, with the AI trade supplying most of the movement. Nvidia beat and guided to $108bn in revenue next quarter, but the same weeks brought scrutiny of how that demand is funded — a $500 billion pledge to its own buyers, a $230 billion backstop of customer lease obligations, and a $21 billion SpaceX stake. Meta took a $17.1bn child-safety settlement, roughly 1% of its stock value.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price American drivers pay at the pump, surveyed weekly across the country. It follows crude, but the gap between the two is refining: when refineries or pipelines falter, pump prices move even when a barrel does not.
us-gas-retail.recent: Fuel markets spent August short of refining, not crude. Ukrainian drones hit Russian plants and Moscow capped station sales at 30 litres, while Putin conceded "not all fuel issues have been resolved" and Russia moved to import fuel and lower standards. India cut its windfall tax on petrol exports to nil, easing supply elsewhere.

natgas-ttf.standing: The price of natural gas at the Dutch TTF hub, the benchmark for gas traded in northwest Europe. It sets what factories, power stations and households pay for heat and electricity, and it moves on pipeline supply, storage levels and weather.
natgas-ttf.recent: The series is monthly and runs to 1 July 2026, so it predates the month's gas news: it rose 47% from a December 2025 low of $9.46 to $17.93 in July, its highest in the window. The coverage since — a second Nord Stream sabotage suspect arrested in Croatia, and Iran's Fars province find of 161 billion cubic meters — postdates the reading.

vix.standing: A measure of how much volatility options traders expect in the S&P 500 over the coming month, derived from the prices they pay for protection. It rises when investors are buying insurance against a fall, which is why it is read as a fear gauge.
vix.recent: Volatility has drained out of markets since the June peak, and the index sits near its 63-day low despite unresolved US-Iran risks and rising sovereign debt. The same calm has settled over crypto, where Bitcoin's volatility collapse has left traders looking elsewhere.

fx-pkr.standing: Pakistan's currency against the dollar, quoted as rupees per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker rupee. It sets the local cost of everything the country imports — fuel, wheat, machinery — and the burden of its dollar-denominated debt.
fx-pkr.recent: The rupee has been close to flat for a month, drifting from 276.6 on Jul 31 to 278.1 on Aug 7 and back to 277.6. The import bill behind it kept growing: Sindh is buying 5 million tons of wheat from abroad, and war-risk costs around Hormuz pushed diesel to 383.95 rupees a litre in mid-August.

fx-ngn.standing: The exchange rate of Nigeria's currency against the US dollar, and the price at which Africa's largest economy imports everything it does not make. It moves on oil earnings, central-bank policy and fuel-import demand, and food and transport prices follow it.
fx-ngn.recent: The naira firmed to 1342 to the dollar, its strongest level in the 30-day window, down from 1365 on Aug 8. Nigeria's Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise called the gains hollow: "Macroeconomic stability is a means, not an end." The APC accused Atiku Abubakar of desperation over his pledge to restore the fuel subsidy, the removal of which underpins the currency's floated rate.

fx-egp.standing: The number of Egyptian pounds it takes to buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel, so the rate sets the price of bread and transport, and the state's dollar debts are paid in a currency it does not print.
fx-egp.recent: The pound moved in a narrow band, from 51.16 on Aug 1 to 49.56 on Aug 8, ending near 50.27 — a move too small to have a single cause in the record. Cairo spent the month as a mediator, hosting Hamas talks on a Gaza withdrawal timetable and discussing de-escalation with Tehran.

fx-try.standing: Turkey's currency, quoted as lira per US dollar, so a rising number means a weaker lira. It is one of the most closely watched emerging-market currencies because its slide has been driven for years by domestic interest-rate policy rather than by outside shocks, and it sets the price of everything Turkey imports.
fx-try.recent: The lira drifted to a fresh low of 48.23 on Aug 28, extending a slow slide from 47.41 on Jul 30 — a move consistent with steady depreciation rather than any single event. Nothing in the month's Turkey news, from the Mecca defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia to the arms transfer to Ukraine that Moscow said 'undermines trust', maps onto the currency's path.

fx-bdt.standing: The exchange rate of Bangladesh's currency against the US dollar. It sets the import cost of fuel, food and industrial inputs for a country whose garment export earnings and worker remittances are both priced in dollars.
fx-bdt.recent: The taka has moved in a narrow band, from 124 on Aug 7 to 122 on Aug 19 and back to 123.1, with no single event behind it. The period covered Bangladesh's post-election settling — Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir elected president on 21 August — and a government panel drafting terms for up to 24 J-10CE jets from China.

fx-idr.standing: Indonesia's currency, quoted as rupiah per US dollar, so a higher number means a weaker rupiah. Southeast Asia's largest economy prices its commodity exports and dollar debt through it, and imported fuel and food costs follow it.
fx-idr.recent: The rupiah strengthened over the month, from 18,070 on Jul 31 to a low of 17,650 on Aug 21, as Prabowo tightened the state's grip on the economy through the cooperatives programme. A magnitude quake in Flores on Aug 16 killed 53 and cut Sikka's coastal road, without visible effect on the currency.

fx-lbp.standing: Lebanon's currency, quoted against the dollar. After the 2019 banking collapse it lost most of its value and now sits at a rate the central bank holds steady, so the number moves less than the economy behind it does.
fx-lbp.recent: The pound barely moved over the month, holding near 89,550 while the war did not: Israeli strikes killed 11 in Lebanon on 17 August and seven near Ansar on 15 August, and the health ministry put the death toll from Israeli attacks at 4,350 by 25 August.

fx-cny.standing: The exchange rate between China's currency and the US dollar, managed within a band the People's Bank of China sets each morning. It is the price at which the world's largest manufacturing base sells, so it moves export prices, and every peer currency in Asia trades around it.
fx-cny.recent: The yuan drifted to its strongest level of the month, 6.721 per dollar on 28 August, after a 30-day range that topped out at 6.762 on 30 July — a move of well under one percent, which is the ordinary width of the managed band rather than a break from it. Nothing in the month's news explains a shift that small.

fx-inr.standing: The exchange rate of India's currency against the dollar, the price at which the world's most populous country buys its imported oil, chips and machinery. A weaker rupee raises the cost of everything India brings in and eases the cost of what it sells abroad.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee held in a narrow band near 95 to the dollar through August, drifting from 95.05 on Aug 5 to a high of 95.77 on Aug 20 before settling at 95.54. Nothing in the month's news explains the move: the trade stories were structural rather than market-moving, from Piyush Goyal taking 200 firms to Japan for semiconductor inputs to the plan to privatise 11 airports in five paired bundles.

fx-brl.standing: Brazil's currency, quoted as reais per dollar, so a higher number means a weaker real. It is one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies, and its swings pass through to Brazilian import costs, inflation and the country's dollar-denominated debt.
fx-brl.recent: The real drifted weaker across the month, from 5.077 on Aug 3 to a high of 5.222 on Aug 15 before settling near 5.163. Nothing in the month's Brazil news — Petrobras detecting oil off the Amazon coast, the banking-hack arrests spanning Germany and Brazil — accounts for the move.

fx-mxn.standing: The Mexican peso against the US dollar, one of the most heavily traded emerging-market currencies. Mexico sends most of its exports north, so the rate moves with US trade policy, US interest rates and the tone of relations between the two governments.
fx-mxn.recent: The peso strengthened from 17.46 on Jul 30 to 16.92 on Aug 21, its firmest level of the month, and sits at 16.97. Washington cancelled Andrés Manuel López Beltrán's US visa on Aug 14, and Claudia Sheinbaum slammed the US over the revocation, but the friction left no mark on the currency.

fx-eur.standing: The price of one euro in US dollars, quoted here inverted as euros per dollar. It is the world's second-most traded currency pair, and the rate sets the cost of every transatlantic invoice, tourist bill and cross-border bond coupon.
fx-eur.recent: The euro strengthened against the dollar through August, with the pair reaching 0.8556 on Aug 20 before easing back. Nothing in the month's European news — the EU's broadest Russia sanctions package, the reopened debate over Russia's frozen billions, or Apple's App Store fee cuts — accounts for the move.

fx-jpy.standing: Japan's currency, quoted as yen per dollar, and one of the world's most traded. A higher number means a weaker yen, which lifts the earnings of Japan's exporters and raises the cost of the energy and food the country imports.
fx-jpy.recent: The yen has firmed from its 163.5 low point on Jul 30 to 159.4, moving with the dollar, which fell against the euro on Aug 17 as markets trimmed rate hike bets. The month's Japan news sat outside currency markets: Putin's visit to the disputed Kuril Islands and a Russian missile test there after Tokyo's protest, and torrential rains that killed eight.

fx-rub.standing: Russia's currency, quoted as rubles per dollar, so a rising number means a weaker ruble. It carries the price of oil and gas revenue into the domestic economy, and it is the cleanest market read on how tightly sanctions are biting.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble slid through August as the war widened rather than wound down: Kremlin sources declared the peace talks dead, Russia struck nine Ukrainian cities overnight, and Moscow opened early voting in occupied Donbas. Washington named nearly 60 entities on Monday, extending the squeeze to third countries that still trade with Russia.

fx-zar.standing: The currency of South Africa, and one of the most heavily traded in the emerging world. It is a proxy trade for global risk appetite and for metals prices, so it moves on decisions made far from Pretoria as much as on those made in it.
fx-zar.recent: The rand has firmed through August, from 16.67 on Jul 30 to a low of 15.92 on Aug 26, a move of about four percent. The domestic news in this window is fiscal rather than monetary — Treasury eyeing R88.6bn in unclaimed accounts and pensions, and NSFAS improperly funding 40,000 students R5.1 billion — and none of it explains the currency.

btc.standing: The largest cryptocurrency by market value, priced against the dollar on exchanges that trade around the clock. It has no cash flows and no issuer, so its price is a fairly direct reading of how much risk capital is willing to hold something backed only by demand for it.
btc.recent: The rise from $62,770 on Aug 2 was a short squeeze rather than a leveraged rally: open interest collapsed as positions were forced shut, carrying Bitcoin to $80,020 and a 23.7% week. The move ran into Warsh's Jackson Hole debut and a White House meeting with crypto CEOs, while BlackRock cut its swap-in threshold from $25 million to $1 million.

eth.standing: The native token of the Ethereum network, the largest platform for smart contracts and the settlement layer beneath most stablecoins, decentralised exchanges and tokenised assets. It is bought both as an asset and to pay for computation on the chain.
eth.recent: The rise came alongside a regulatory thaw: the US securities regulator proposed a crypto rulebook on 23 August after scrapping an earlier Reg Crypto vote, and Wall Street put $11.2 billion into licensed crypto firms in six months. In Seoul, Mirae's Park Hyeon-joo set a $109 billion target for a bank-owned exchange.

paxg.standing: A token backed one-for-one by physical gold, so it tracks the metal's spot price. Gold is what money moves into when currencies, banks or governments look unreliable, and it pays nothing — its only return is the price.
paxg.recent: The series rose 12% over the month to a peak of $4,672 on Aug 25. The input does not explain the move: the gold stories in the window are local ones — Kassala's street dealers outbidding the licensed market, and mineral rents funding M23's hold on North Kivu — not drivers of the global price.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: A count of how many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It rises when the technology reaches people who do not follow it professionally, so it tracks public curiosity rather than industry activity.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: The 14 August peak came as Apple prepared to launch a custom Apple Intelligence model in China and India pushed semiconductor plants under Modi's self-reliance drive. Readership has since fallen back, even as Bill Gates warned of a turbulent transition and reversed his January view that AI would destroy far fewer jobs.

wiki-russia.standing: The Wikipedia article on Russia, and a daily count of how many people open it. Read as attention rather than news: it rises when something puts the country in front of people who then go looking for the basics.
wiki-russia.recent: The peak on Aug 17 sat inside a run of escalation: the EU foreign affairs chief moved to expand sanctions against Russia, Ukraine launched one of its largest attacks of the war on Aug 16, and Putin visited the disputed Kurils on Aug 18, prompting Russia to summon Japan's ambassador. Missiles killed at least 13 in Kyiv on Aug 20.

wiki-pakistan.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Pakistan, a rough gauge of how many people worldwide are looking the country up on any given day. It rises when Pakistan is at the centre of a story and falls back when it is not.

wiki-china.standing: The daily count of people opening the English Wikipedia article on China — a rough gauge of how much of the world is trying to read up on the country, rather than any measure of the country itself.
wiki-china.recent: The 13 August peak sat between two China stories: China ordered a recall of 3 million Teslas over flush door handles, a design 60% of China's best-selling EVs also use, and the country delayed its crewed Moon landing citing "ensuring absolute success". Attention held into late August as a landslide-dammed barrier lake formed in Gyirong County above Nepal's Rasuwagadhi valley, where flood deaths reached at least 160.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: The sea lane between Iran and Oman that connects the Gulf to the Indian Ocean, and the narrowest point in the world's oil trade. Roughly a fifth of seaborne crude and a third of LNG pass through it, so what stops there is felt by importers first.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Readership tracked the strait's closure by insurance rather than by force. The 18 August peak followed an unknown projectile striking a vessel's engine room off Muscat, killing one crew member; traffic had already fallen to six ships on the Tuesday before, and to a single gas carrier by 25 August. Iran's Rezaei then tied reopening to Gaza.

wiki-india.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on India, a proxy for how many people worldwide are looking up the country rather than a particular story about it. It rises when India is doing something that sends strangers to a reference page.
wiki-india.recent: The peak on Aug 15 was India's 80th Independence Day, marked with celebrations across the country and a Modi speech renewing the push for 'aatmanirbhar Bharat' — semiconductor plants, energy security, 650 new universities since 2014. Attention has since slid to a low on Aug 23, with the tail carried by flash flooding near the Nepal-China border that killed at least 95 and left 288 Indians missing.

wiki-ukraine.standing: A count of how many people open the English Wikipedia article on Ukraine each day. It rises when the war forces itself back into general attention, so it tracks public interest rather than events on the ground.
wiki-ukraine.recent: The 24 August peak came as Ukraine's allies convened in Kyiv and Zelenskyy said Patriot deliveries have halved since 2023, with Britain lifting its veto on MBDA sharing SCALP missile component data. Attention had already been raised by Russian missiles killing at least 13 in Kyiv on 20 August and NABU agents searching Zelenskyy's own office.

wiki-nigeria.standing: Daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Nigeria, Africa's most populous country and its largest economy. The count rises when events there pull outside attention, and falls back to a steady baseline of routine lookups.
wiki-nigeria.recent: Attention held highest around Osun state's election, where civil society groups tallied 56 incidents and 14 deaths, and Adeleke's re-election drew congratulations from Atiku, Obi, Kwankwaso and Saraki. It has drained since, through Atiku's pledge to restore the petrol subsidy in 2027 and Tinubu's suspension of three permanent secretaries.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Traffic has collapsed to a handful of vessels a day — one gas carrier on Monday — after Iran's Rezaei warned that "not even one drop" would leave Hormuz and tied resumption to an end to the war in Gaza. A temporary corridor charted with Oman, and Trump's declaration that the strait is clear, have not restored insurable passage. Bahrain's output shrank 3.8%.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: Traffic sits well below its own 90-day baseline after a Houthi missile hit a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu, and the Houthis said they attacked a vessel off Saudi Arabia. Saudi Arabia shelled villages in Yemen's Razih district the same week, with no sign of the shipping war narrowing. Seas were calm, at 0.4m.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: Traffic remains thin: 37 vessels a day against a high of 57 on Aug 11, with the Red Sea still a live theatre — the Houthis said they attacked a vessel off Saudi Arabia on Aug 24, and Pakistani nationals injured in an earlier Houthi attack in the Red Sea returned home. Egypt and Iran's foreign ministers discussed de-escalation on Aug 23.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: Traffic has run about 8% below its own 90-day baseline, with the low of 170 vessels a day on Jul 19 well under the Jun 22 high of 264. The input names no closure or weather event at the strait itself — wave heights peaked at 0.6m — and the Houthi missile strike on a Saudi tanker off Yanbu sits on a different route.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: Transits are running 3.7% below their own 90-day baseline, with daily counts swinging from 28 vessels on 10 July to 401 two days later. The window covers a sharpening standoff over Taiwan and chip supply: Taipei indicted nine people including an Nvidia manager over AI server smuggling, Washington moved on chip tariffs, and Wang Yi told Washington to "remove disruptions" ahead of a summit. Waves stayed modest at 1.8 metres.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: Transits have run about 13 percent below their 90-day baseline, and the canal has moved to cap daily transits in anticipation of a severe El Niño — the weather pattern that drains the lake the locks draw on. Separately, CK Hutchison is seeking HK$11.7 billion from Panama over the canal ports dispute.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Traffic has thinned as the Black Sea shipping war widened: TASS says Russia struck 130 ships since July, and a third Greek vessel in three days burned on 18 August. Turkey says it is not in contact with Russia on a moratorium on military operations in the Black Sea. Grain and oil sailings carry the cost.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Traffic has run about 5.8 percent below its 90-day baseline, with no weather to explain it: waves peaked at 1.3 metres. The pressure is regulatory rather than physical, as Treasury named nearly 60 entities under the "Economic Outcast" campaign and Iran's Rezaei warned that "not even one drop" would leave Hormuz, pushing owners and insurers to re-check routes.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.
cp:dover.recent: Traffic through the strait is running about 6.5% below its own 90-day baseline, with 154 vessels a day against a high of 186 on Aug 1 and a low of 126 on Aug 3. Nothing in the record explains the drop: waves peaked at a modest 2.1m and no weather alert was in force.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: Diversions around the Cape have eased back toward normal after the July peak of 123 vessels a day, with the latest reading of 84 running level with its own 90-day baseline. The Houthi missile strike on a Saudi supertanker off Yanbu on 24 August has not yet pushed traffic back onto the long route.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: Traffic has stopped: the strait recorded zero vessels a day on 23 August, 97 percent below its own 90-day baseline, after a June high of 25. The shutdown runs alongside an intensifying war on the coast it serves — Russia struck nine Ukrainian cities on 27 August, Kremlin sources declared the peace talks dead, and Moscow opened early voting in occupied Ukrainian territory.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Arab world’s largest exchange by market value, dominated by Aramco. Trades Sunday to Thursday, so it opens the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: The index closed at its 36-day high on 26 August, the day a Washington nuclear agreement was reported to await Saudi recognition of Israel, and the enrichment clause was left in. Two days earlier Riyadh signed a joint defence pact with Pakistan and Turkey in Mecca, shelled villages in Razih district in Saada, and Houthis said they attacked a vessel off Saudi Arabia.

mkt:bist.standing: Türkiye’s only exchange. Priced in lira, so its index level carries the country’s inflation as much as its earnings — read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: The index sits near the top of its 63-day range after a low on Jul 30, through a month in which Turkey's foreign policy dominated the news: a joint defence pact signed with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia whose terms were not made public, 70 long-range US missiles routed to Ukraine via Turkey over Moscow's objections, and Israeli strikes on an air base in Syria's Idlib near the Turkish border.

mkt:dfm.standing: The Gulf’s main listing venue for property and banking. Moved from a Sunday–Thursday week to Monday–Friday in 2022, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The index sits well below its Jun 18 high of 6270 after Iran fired two ballistic missiles at the UAE on 18 August, triggering Dubai's first emergency alert in months, and the UAE responded by suspending all trade and financial transactions with Iran. Two ADNOC tankers were struck transiting Hormuz days earlier, and 137,000 Gulf tourism jobs are forecast lost.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The world’s largest market for Islamic finance instruments, and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The index reached 1749 on Aug 26, then slipped as prosecutors charged former prime minister Ismail Sabri Yaakob with concealing assets. He pleaded not guilty in the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court to failing to declare tens of millions of dollars — the third Malaysian ex-premier charged after leaving office, after Najib Razak and Muhyiddin Yassin.

mkt:idx.standing: The exchange of the world’s largest Muslim-majority country, heavily weighted to commodities and banking.
mkt:idx.recent: The index has climbed to 6,542 from a 5,342 low on Jun 8, its high coming as Prabowo tightened the state's grip on the economy through cooperatives, and as Jakarta pushed to classify millions of ride-hailing drivers as "partners" rather than employees. A quake in Flores that killed 53 severed Sikka's coastal road but left the market unmoved.

mkt:tse.standing: Asia’s largest exchange, and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: The index sits at 66,600, up 2.9% across the window but well below its 25 June high of 72,370 and recovering from a 29 July low of 61,430. The input does not explain what drove those swings.

mkt:hkex.standing: Where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital — the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range after recovering from a Jun 26 low of 22670. Wang Yi told Washington to "remove disruptions" ahead of a summit, while Beijing ordered a recall of 3 million Teslas over flush door handles and moved to export its own supply-chain and due-diligence standards.

mkt:sse.standing: Mainland China’s main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, so it tracks domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The index sits near 3960 after a 3.4% slide from its 4163 high on Jun 22, with the trough at 3764 on Jul 17. Nothing in the record explains the drift, though it spans a stretch in which Beijing told Washington to "remove disruptions" before a summit, ordered a recall of 3 million Teslas, and moved to export its own supply-chain and due-diligence standards.

mkt:krx.standing: Dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix — a proxy for the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: The Bank of Korea hiked rates to 3.00% on 27 August, the chip cycle setting the pace, and the index has given back 16% from its 22 June high of 9,115. Washington's cancellation of next month's Twin Dragons exercise landed alongside Lee's push to replace the armistice with a peace treaty.

mkt:bse.standing: Asia’s oldest exchange, founded 1875, and the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: The index sits near the top of its 65-day range after a run of policy and privatisation news out of New Delhi: India moved to privatise 11 airports in five paired bundles, and OpenAI opened ChatGPT advertising in India with 50 brands, treating the country as a test market. Modi has renewed his push for semiconductor plants and energy security.

mkt:sgx.standing: Southeast Asia’s financial hub, weighted to banks and regional property.
mkt:sgx.recent: The index has climbed 13.93% over the past 64 days to a high of 5768 on Aug 17, with Singapore's role as a regional financial hub in evidence: crypto card spending tripled to $1.04 billion, and a 70-member Indian delegation arrived on Aug 19 for talks on tech, investment and trade ties.

mkt:twse.standing: TSMC alone is roughly a third of the index, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: The index has recovered 6.52% over the past 65 days from its Jul 30 low of 39930, closing at 46480. The window has been thick with pressure on Taiwan rather than relief: China's coast guard now patrols east of Taiwan, Indonesian warships drilled with China's navy there, and Taiwan indicted nine people including an Nvidia manager.

mkt:set.standing: Thailand’s benchmark, sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The index sits near the top of its 38-day range after climbing from a 1541 low on Jun 23 to 1639 on Jul 17, though it fell about 2% on the latest session. Bangkok's diplomatic realignment toward Moscow has been the running story, with Russia-Thailand trade up 23% in January-May 2026 and a Thai deputy prime minister seeking cybersecurity cooperation with Russia.

mkt:pse.standing: A small, domestically-driven market where remittance flows move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: The index sits at its 37-day high after a 7.4% run from its late-May low, and the political news out of Manila has not dented it: an ex-disbursing officer told the Senate impeachment court that Duterte ordered a P125-million confidential funds transfer. Nothing in that testimony touches the listed companies the index tracks.

mkt:asx.standing: Mining and banking. Often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The index sits near the top of its three-month range, about 5.5% above its late-May low, having peaked at 9272 on 6 August before easing back. The clearest domestic signal in the window came ahead of inflation data on 18 August, with the professional-services sector under visible strain as KPMG Australia cut 27 partners and 360 staff.

mkt:jse.standing: Africa’s largest exchange by far, and the continent’s only one with a usable public daily series.

mkt:b3.standing: Latin America’s largest exchange, driven by iron ore, oil and Brazilian rates.
mkt:b3.recent: The index is roughly flat over the window, sliding from its Aug 3 high to an Aug 18 low before recovering. Two Brazilian bank stories bracket the dip: arrests in Germany and Brazil over a banking hack on Aug 14, and the Bank Master fraud case, where organised crime groups and militias are among the accused alongside bankers and politicians. Petrobras reported signs of oil off the Amazon coast on Aug 17.

mkt:bmv.standing: Mexico’s benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The index has fallen roughly 6% over the period, sliding from 70,020 on May 27 to a low of 63,930 on Aug 18 and closing at 65,830. The clearest political shock in the window was Washington's cancellation of Andrés Manuel López Beltrán's US visa, which Claudia Sheinbaum publicly condemned, against a wider backdrop of Trump's cross-border trade fights.

mkt:byma.standing: Priced in a currency that has lost most of its value repeatedly, so the index rises even in bad years. Direction over a day means something; the level does not.
mkt:byma.recent: The index sits below its late-July peak of 3,380,000 after sliding to 2,874,000 on Aug 19. The material here does not explain the move: the Buenos Aires news in the window concerns an Interpol operation that dismantled a fraud network, with 58 arrested and 196 identified, and the arrest of a Milei adviser over the shooting of a lawyer.

mkt:tsx.standing: Energy, mining and banks — a commodity index wearing an equity index’s clothes.
mkt:tsx.recent: The index held near its high through the breakdown of Canada-US trade talks: Washington imposed new tariffs on 22 August, Ottawa answered dollar for dollar with a list taxing perfume, golf clubs and video consoles, and Ontario Premier Doug Ford threatened to cut power exports. Energy and mining weightings absorbed the shock.

mkt:nyse.standing: The largest equity market on earth. Its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: The index sits near the 7,799 high it reached on 13 August, up about 2% over the window from a 7,267 low on 10 June, with a 0.72% gain on the day. Trade and sanctions policy dominated the period: Canada matched US tariffs dollar-for-dollar on a list taxing perfume, golf clubs and video consoles, and Washington widened sanctions aimed at isolating Iran's economy.

mkt:lse.standing: Most FTSE 100 revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The index sits near the high of 10,910 it reached on Jul 29, up on the series despite a 0.8% fall on the day. The domestic news of the window was political rather than financial: Nigel Farage's Clacton by-election win on 14 August, and Russia's warning on 27 August that Britain is 'playing with fire' over Ukraine.

mkt:xetra.standing: Germany’s industrial and chemical base — Europe’s clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The index sits near its 67-day peak of 26,440 on Aug 14, and the coverage in that window is mostly non-market: the EU's plan for its broadest Russia sanctions package, a second Nord Stream arrest in Croatia, and a malaria death among Frankfurt Airport workers. None of that explains the 4.4% climb from the Jun 10 low.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: Luxury goods and energy dominate — unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: The index sits near the top of its range after a run of French industrial and space policy news: the European Space Agency awarded €544 million to three rocket startups on 27 August, and said it would adapt Ariane 6 for future Argonaut landers. The single-day drop of 1.7% is not explained by anything in the record.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The world’s oldest exchange, now carried largely by ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: The index has climbed to 1108, roughly 5% higher across the window, with the peak of 1120 on 13 August and no single Dutch event in view to explain the run. The daily move is flat, down 0.145%.

mkt:bme.standing: Spanish banks with heavy Latin American exposure make this a proxy for both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: The index sits near the top of its 67-day range after climbing from a June low, with Spain's decision to extend the life of its largest nuclear plant in a policy U-turn removing a scheduled shutdown from utility planning. The move on 27 August pared the level from the 11 August high.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: Banks and utilities, and the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The index sits near the top of its 67-day range after climbing roughly 5 percent since late May, with the high on Aug 7 and a drop of about 1.2 percent on the latest day. The input carries no Italian market news to explain the move.

mkt:six.standing: Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry the index, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: Nordic industrials and telecoms, and a useful early read on European capital spending.
mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.recent: The index gained about 5 percent over the window, reaching 3,327 on Aug 5 after a low of 3,054 on Jun 10, and has drifted slightly since. The available material does not explain what drove the move.

mkt:tase.standing: Trades Sunday to Thursday. Heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The index is down 8.5% across the 66-day window, sliding from a high of 4433 on May 27 to a low of 3966 on Jun 29. It has clawed back part of that ground since, sitting at 4043. Nothing in the available material explains the decline.

xag.standing: A silver-backed token whose price tracks an ounce of physical silver held in vaulted allocated bullion. Silver is both a monetary metal and an industrial input — solar cells, electronics and brazing all compete for the same supply.
xag.recent: The series more than doubled off its $29.81 low on Aug 6 to $69.42 on Aug 28, a 17.93% rise across the window. The input carries no supply, policy or demand event that accounts for the move.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate untouched at the next meeting. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves as rate-sensitive borrowing, mortgage and currency costs come into view.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: The contract climbed from 39 on Aug 1 to a high of 75 on Aug 15, settling at 69. Fed minutes released on Aug 19 showed many officials said rate hikes may be needed, which cut against a hold and trimmed the price from its peak. Polymarket itself has been under pressure, with South Korea joining more than 30 jurisdictions restricting access.

wiki-petroleum.standing: A refined product benchmark and the raw material behind fuel, plastics and fertiliser. Its price sets the cost of moving almost everything, which is why a strike, a sanction or a closed strait shows up in freight and food weeks later.
wiki-petroleum.recent: Readership tracked the pressure on two producers. The rise into 13 August came as Washington moved toward the 'toughest sanctions' on Iran, with Tehran vowing to resist and shipping traffic in Hormuz slowing to a near halt; Putin conceded that 'not all fuel issues have been resolved' in Russia. Washington is now negotiating a stake in Venezuelan oil.

poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether U.S. forces launch a ground invasion of Iran before 2027. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, so it moves with escalation and with anything that makes an economic route look more likely than a military one.
poly-will-the-us-invade-iran-before-2027.recent: Odds halved from 26 percent on Aug 2 as Washington shifted to money. Treasury Secretary Bessent named the campaign "Economic Outcast" and Treasury listed nearly 60 entities Monday, binding third countries; the rial opened at 2.02 million per dollar. Rezaei's threat that "not even one drop" leaves Hormuz gave way to a temporary corridor charted with Oman.

wiki-syria.standing: The Wikipedia country article for Syria, and one of the steadiest gauges of how much of the world is looking at it. Readership sits flat for months and then jumps within a day of a strike, a verdict or a change of government.
wiki-syria.recent: The 11 August peak sits just before a dense run of Syrian news: on 18 August eight strikes hit an airbase in Idlib, Syria granted the IAEA access to an Assad-era undeclared nuclear site concealed for 18 years, and a court sentenced Wassim al-Assad to death. Trump then removed Syria from the terrorism list on 24 August.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The daily readership of the English Wikipedia article on Donald Trump — a rough gauge of how many people are looking up the sitting US president rather than a measure of anything he does. It rises when a decision, a ruling or a confrontation sends people to check the record.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: The late-August peak tracked a widening campaign against Iran: sanctions Tehran vowed to resist, a Hormuz strait Trump declared clear that had not reopened, and a Saudi nuclear deal left without an enrichment ban. Earlier in the month the Supreme Court denied his Carroll appeal without comment, and Canada matched US tariffs dollar for dollar.

poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.standing: A prediction market on whether Brazil's incumbent president wins the country's 2026 general election. Traders buy and sell contracts that settle on the result, so the price is what money will pay for that outcome, not a poll.
poly-will-luiz-incio-lula-da-silva-win-t.recent: The contract has drifted down from 67% on Aug 2 to 57% on Aug 28, its low over the past month, without a single event in the window accounting for the slide.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Benjamin Netanyahu will be Israel's next prime minister — that is, whether he holds the office after the next change of government. It is a live gauge of how traders read his coalition's durability and his personal legal and political exposure.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: The price fell from 37 on Aug 2 to 25, over a month in which Netanyahu's position drew external pressure rather than domestic wins: Kushner met Hamas leaders in Cairo and then Netanyahu to push the Trump Gaza plan, European powers rebuked Israel over the E1 settlement plan, and Turkey moved to seek an Interpol notice for him over the Gaza flotilla case.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction, unlike bitcoin's public ledger. That privacy is why it is the settlement asset of choice for ransomware and sanctions evasion, and why exchanges keep delisting it.
xmr.recent: The price rose about a third over the month to its high on Aug 28, tracking a run of ransomware and sanctions news: CISA identified more than 200 Medusa victims over the last year, a Ukrainian software developer went on trial in Bellinzona facing 12 years, and North Korea's sanctions evasion toolkit now earns revenue without touching banks.

wiki-stablecoin.standing: A crypto token designed to hold a fixed value, usually one dollar, by holding reserves against every coin issued. It is the settlement layer crypto trades on, and the reason banks and card networks now argue over who issues the money that moves.
wiki-stablecoin.recent: Attention followed the institutions moving in rather than the technology: Standard Chartered began distributing Hong Kong's dollar stablecoin, Shinhan started building won stablecoin rails with a card network, and 39 state banking associations announced a rival chain to defend deposits. Crypto card spending tripled to $1.04 billion.

wiki-united-states.standing: Daily readership of Wikipedia's article on the United States. It rises when the country itself becomes the story — an election, a strike, a policy that reaches beyond its borders — and is one of the few free measures of where global attention sits.
wiki-united-states.recent: The window is bracketed by Washington's pressure campaign on Iran: Treasury Secretary Bessent named the sanctions effort "Economic Outcast" and moved to bind third countries, while Iran's Rezaei warned that "not even one drop" would leave Hormuz. Reading peaked on Aug 15, the day multiple people were shot at Virginia State University.

wiki-bitcoin.standing: The pageview count for Wikipedia's Bitcoin article — a rough gauge of how many people are looking the asset up on any given day. It rises when the price moves hard enough, or the rules around it change enough, to pull in readers who do not follow it daily.
wiki-bitcoin.recent: The 24 August peak followed a violent week in the price: Bitcoin surged to $80,020, up 23.7%, in what turned out to be a short squeeze rather than a leveraged rally, with $48 billion of futures open against $25 billion in daily volume. Institutional access widened alongside it — BlackRock cut its swap-in threshold from $25 million to $1 million.
